headline: The main drug used
body: has a side effect profile nobody measures in the people taking it for height.
punch: Not because it's safe. Because nobody looked.

headline: Aromatase inhibitors
body: Letrozole and anastrozole block testosterone converting into estrogen. Less estrogen means slower bone maturation, and in boys that means more adult height.
punch: That part is well documented. It's the monitoring that isn't.

headline: The same drugs
body: In postmenopausal breast cancer, aromatase inhibitors are standard therapy — often for years. That population has been studied intensively for adverse effects.
punch: Which means we know exactly what to look for.

headline: And there
body: Arthralgia and myalgia. Altered retinal function. Subtle negative effects on verbal and visual memory in some patients. The brain makes its own estrogen, and these drugs block that too.
punch: The brain isn't collateral damage. It's an aromatase-expressing organ.

headline: Now the gap
body: Paediatric height-therapy studies of these drugs generally don't screen for the sensory or cognitive outcomes that oncology treats as standard safety monitoring.
punch: A median 25 months of treatment with no cognitive endpoints recorded.

headline: There is one reassurance
body: A single line in the literature says letrozole doesn't impair cognitive development in boys. That's one citation, not a monitoring programme.
punch: One reassuring sentence is not the same as having measured it.

headline: It might genuinely be fine
body: A developing brain may compensate differently than an ageing one. That's a plausible explanation for why the oncology findings might not transfer.
punch: Plausible. Also completely untested in this population.

headline: So the honest position
body: Effective for height in the right clinical context, under supervision. And carrying a documented adverse-effect profile that the height literature has not looked for.
punch: Absence of reported harm isn't evidence of absence. Nobody was measuring.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
